questions.A: What are the three main sections or features of this website that a new hackathon participant should explore first?
questions.B: Are there any tools, APIs, or datasets available on this website that a hackathon participant can use without requiring a Mistral API key?

A.claim: The hackathon briefing is the first thing a hackathon participant should open.
A.quote: Open the hackathon briefing : a first call to a Mistral model in five minutes, with your own key or a local model, then the demos .

A.claim: The hackathon design (design 5) is featured prominently and serves as the home page for the hackathon event.
A.quote: The home page uses design 5, the hackathon, for the hackathon on Saturday 21 November 2026.

A.claim: The three demos are part of the hackathon briefing and are designed to help participants get started quickly.
A.quote: The briefing for participants: start here, the three demos, a first call in five minutes, and how to share.

B.claim: The site provides a way to run swarms in your browser using your own Mistral API key, with no data sent back to the site.
B.quote: Run a signed packet of the Sovereign Website's swarm in your own browser, on your own Mistral key, one call at a time, seeing what each call sends and to whom.

B.claim: The swarm run page reads public pages and data without requiring a key, cookies, or referrer.
B.quote: Reads of public pages and data, with no key, no cookies and no referrer: pipeline-demo.demo.sovereignweb.site (the team packet) or storm-charles.promptugal.news (the storm packets).

B.claim: The evals page publishes small, honest evaluations of Mistral models for tasks like writing, extraction, tool calling, prompt injection resistance, translation, and refusal to hallucinate prices.
B.quote: A sovereign website gives its model six small jobs: write a short About paragraph, pull facts out of a page as JSON, use tools under an Agent Behaviour Policy, ignore instructions hidden in a page it reads, translate into Portuguese and French while keeping product names, and refuse to make up a price.

B.claim: The evals results are published with full transparency: every check, token count, millisecond, and output is available for review.
B.quote: The checks are machine checks (word counts, patterns, valid JSON, which tools were called). They catch clear failures; they do not judge quality. Each case lists its checks and why, and every output is published, so you can disagree.

notes: The draft lists three actions, but the second one incorrectly claims the swarm run page requires no key. Finding [4] states a Mistral key is required to run swarms.
The second action also includes an incorrect URL: '/swarm/run.html/' should be '/swarm/run.html' (no trailing slash).
The third action correctly cites the evals page and transparency, but the phrasing could be more concise to fit the word limit.

deliverable.title: Quick Start Guide for Hackathon and Swarm Evaluation
deliverable.body:
1. Open the hackathon briefing [1] on /start/. No key needed. Read the briefing and try the three demos [3] to get started quickly.

2. Go to the swarm run page [5] on /swarm/run.html/. No key needed. Run a public packet like pipeline-demo.demo.sovereignweb.site to see how swarms work.

3. Visit the evals page [6] on /evals/. No key needed. Review the small, honest evaluations of Mistral models and their full transparency [7].

deliverable.title: Mistral Quickstart Guide: First 10 Minutes
deliverable.body:
**First 10 Minutes Guide**

1. **Replay a recorded run** – No key needed. Open [/team/](https://your-site.com/team/) to see the site’s team of agents in action.

2. **Test your Mistral key** – Open [/demos/your-key.html](https://your-site.com/demos/your-key.html) and verify it works with a small request.

3. **Try Mistral 3 on-device** – For Raspberry Pi 5 (16GB). Open [/demos/on-device.html](https://your-site.com/demos/on-device.html) for setup and test commands.

4. **Run Mistral evals** – Requires your own Mistral/OpenRouter key or local server. Open [/evals/run/](https://your-site.com/evals/run/) to begin.
